scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge that occurred 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Claire Sullivan and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, I see. Can you tell me your name and age again? I need to make sure I'm looking at the right account.
As I just said, I'm Claire Sullivan and I'm 64.
Right. Well, our policy says 30 days, and you're at 34 days. That's just the rule we have to follow, so I can't really do anything about it.
I understand the policy, but given the circumstances of my travel, is there no flexibility? I've been a loyal customer for years.
Look, I don't make the rules. If you want, I can send this to a supervisor, but they'll probably just tell you the same thing.
Yes, please. I would appreciate it if you could escalate this for me.
Fine. I've opened a ticket for a manager to look at. They'll get back to you whenever they get to it.

escalation_reason: Agent failed to exercise discretionary authority or provide a helpful resolution, instead passing the request to a supervisor due to personal impatience.
